_comment: CROSS-BOUNDARY CONTRACT — the Robertson soil-behaviour-type bands keyed on Ic.
This file is the single arbiter both sides check themselves against. It exists
because a 'parity' test that compared the renderer's band table with a renderer
function that iterates the same table could never go red, while the drift that
actually happened was renderer<->backend: the chart labelled every band one step
too coarse and the backend's classify_soil_ic carried the same shift (audit
Changing a breakpoint or a label means changing it HERE first and watching both
suites go red. Zone 1 (sensitive fine-grained) is deliberately absent: it is read
off the Qtn-Fr chart, not off Ic, so no Ic band may be labelled 'Sensitive'.
ic_max of the last band is null = unbounded above (Ic has no ceiling; the chart
axis stops at 4 for drawing only).

bands.backend_label: Sands: clean sand to silty sand
Sand mixtures: silty sand to sandy silt
Silt mixtures: clayey silt to silty clay

_zones_comment: The NINE Robertson (2009) chart ZONES, as the SBT strips draw them. Distinct
from 'bands' above: a band is an Ic interval, a zone is a position on the
Qtn-Fr chart, so zones 1, 8 and 9 have no Ic interval at all and appear only
here. 'strip_label' is the name the strip and its legend show; 'strip_fill' is
the hue it paints. Both are held to this file by icBands.sbtParity.test.tsx,
so a label reworded or a hue nudged in the renderer goes red here first.
strip_label is DERIVED FROM robertson_2015.sbt_zone_series' docstring, not
copied verbatim: zone 2 is named for peat (it is the zone the extended
Lengkeek & Brinkgreve boundary feeds, and 'organic soil / clay' hides that),
and zones 8/9 lead with 'Very stiff' where the backend puts the qualifier in
parentheses. Those two rewordings are deliberate and this file is where they
Zone 2's #92400e is a DELIBERATE break from the Ic band's amber #fef3c7 for
the same soil: on a 22 px categorical strip the organic run has to be findable
at a glance, and peat brown is the one hue no neighbouring zone competes with.
OWNER-RETINTABLE: if the two surfaces reading differently for one soil bothers
the eye more than a lost organic run does, change the hue HERE and both the
strip and its guard move together.

zones.strip_label: Very stiff sand to clayey sand
